source_file: 10182963_2024_Siguel v. King Farm Citizens Assembly, Inc._mdd
reasoning: Court denied defendant's motion for reconsideration; FHA Count VI (reasonable accommodation) survived and plaintiff's disability discrimination claim proceeds. No pleading failure on the FHA disability claim.
Court denied defendants' motion to dismiss; FHA disability discrimination claim adequately pleaded and proceeds past 12(b)(6). No pleading failure.
Section 1915(e)(2) screening dismissal; plaintiff's FHA disability claim failed to allege specific facts showing discrimination or retaliation tied to disability beyond conclusory assertions.
Dismissal turned on Rooker-Feldman and Younger abstention barring federal adjudication of claims tied to state eviction proceedings, not on pleading deficiencies in the FHA elements.
FHA claim dismissed as time-barred under the two-year statute of limitations; repeat-filer plaintiff could not revive claims tied to events long past the limitations period.
FHA claim failed because complaint lacked facts showing discriminatory intent or disparate impact tied to disability, and failed to establish necessity for the requested accommodation.
Section 1915 screening dismissal; retaliation allegations failed to identify specific protected FHA activity, adverse action, or causal link in terms cognizable under § 3617.
Dismissed for lack of subject matter jurisdiction; bare invocation of FHA without colorable federal claim failed to establish federal question jurisdiction.

source_file: 10657815_2025_Bortnick v. Housing Authority of Lincoln County_ord
reasoning: FHA disability claim dismissed as barred by the statute of limitations; accrual analysis placed conduct outside the limitations window.

source_file: 10697217_2017_Lath v. Oak Brook Condominium Owners Assoc., et al._nhd
reasoning: § 3617 retaliation counts dismissed for failure to allege animus tied to a protected characteristic on part of defendants who engaged in the challenged conduct; § 3604(f)(2) ANSI-based claim dismissed for lack of standing because plaintiff did not allege he had a physical handicap or was denied accessible parking.

source_file: 10740678_2025_John R. Fouts v. United States of America et al._kywd
reasoning: Section 1915 screening; FHA allegations conclusory and lacked facts supporting a cognizable discrimination theory tied to a protected class.

source_file: 10766941_2025_Valery Kantsepolsky v. River Shores Association, Inc._flsd
reasoning: FHA disability claim survived 12(b)(6); court stayed the federal action under Colorado River abstention but did not dismiss for pleading failure. The claim was adequately pleaded on the merits.

source_file: 10805479_2026_Jlyn Bryant et al. v. Tinker Federal Credit Union_okwd
reasoning: FHA/ECOA claims grounded in 'vapor money' theory failed to plead membership in a protected class, comparator treatment, or facts tying any adverse action to a protected characteristic.

source_file: 11267609 - Doria v. YAVAPAI COLLEGE DISTRICT GOVERNING BOARD
reasoning: Dismissal rested on res judicata and collateral estoppel from prior litigation of the same or related claims, barring relitigation rather than turning on the adequacy of disability allegations.

Third Circuit held that the requested accommodation was not plausibly 'necessary' under § 3604(f)(3)(B) in light of alternatives available; failure lay in the necessity element, not the factual narrative.

source_file: 9526612_2023_Allfrey v. Fairhope Motorcoach Resort Condominium Owners Association, Inc._alsd
reasoning: FHA disability claim failed because plaintiff did not allege conduct by defendants that constituted discrimination on the basis of disability or denial of a reasonable accommodation connected to defendants' acts.

Case dismissed on combined grounds: failure to state an FHA claim (no cognizable housing-discrimination theory against a non-housing defendant) and failure to prosecute, constituting multiple independent bases.
§ 3617 claim was inapposite because the dispute involved a market/storefront and non-housing conduct; plaintiff's allegations did not translate into any cognizable FHA dwelling-related theory.

Case dismissed under Rooker-Feldman; FHA § 3617 claim not independent of state-court eviction orders, so the federal court lacked subject matter jurisdiction. Dismissal did not rest on FHA pleading adequacy.

Court identified that plaintiff did not allege he or his partner had a qualifying disability or facts linking defendants' conduct to disability discrimination under the FHA; motion denied with leave to amend, but the identified deficiency was factual underdevelopment.

source_file: 9742964_2024_Affinity Recovery Center LLC v. Town Commissioners of Sudlersville_mdd
reasoning: FHA discrimination and reasonable-accommodation claims dismissed because complaint failed to show the 8-bed zoning rule singled out substance-use disabilities and failed to show expansion to 16 beds was 'necessary' under Bryant Woods Inn.
FHA disability claim dismissed because plaintiff alleged discrimination in conclusory terms and supplied no factual support for any element of the claim.
Section 1915 screening; complaint parroted FHA elements without identifying any cognizable theory (disparate treatment, disparate impact, or reasonable accommodation) or tying conduct to facts.

Plaintiff won judgment on the pleadings on her procedural due process claim and obtained the relief she sought (order directing an informal hearing); the FHA/ADA/Section 504 claims were dismissed as moot, not for pleading failure.

FHA § 3604(f)(2) and § 3617 claims dismissed because allegations of inadequate care/negligence did not establish discriminatory animus, intentional disparate treatment, or retaliation; claims attacked adequacy of services rather than discrimination.

FHA claim against real estate agency dismissed because single-sentence allegation that apartment was denied because son has autism lacked factual detail (when, where, why) needed for a minimal inference of discriminatory motivation.

Third amended complaint dismissed with prejudice for repeated noncompliance with Rule 8 and court orders to provide a short and plain statement; substance of FHA claim never reached because of form defects.

FHA claim dismissed because complaint alleged HUD's failure to intervene against PHA/neighbors, conduct not covered by § 3604(f); no cognizable disability-discrimination theory could be constructed from the facts alleged.

FHA/FHAA claim dismissed without prejudice because plaintiff did not plead membership in a protected class, did not tie conduct to disability discrimination, and did not allege a refused reasonable accommodation.

FHA race and disability claims dismissed because complaint failed to draw a sufficient nexus between handicap/race and defendants' actions; no facts showed housing denial or adverse treatment was because of handicap.
